rationale: Evidence from genetic models of TUBA4A-associated spastic ataxia (SPAX11) confirms that post-developmental Purkinje neuron degeneration directly drives cerebellar atrophy and progressive ataxic manifestations. In Tuba4aQ176P mutant models, mice exhibit normal early cerebellar development at 3 weeks, followed by rapid, time-dependent degeneration of Purkinje cells alongside cerebellar atrophy and overt ataxia by 30 days. Clinical and cohort reports in humans (harboring missense variants including p.Glu415Lys and de novo mutations) demonstrate progressive spastic ataxia with cerebellar degeneration and atrophy. While other tubulinopathies (e.g., TUBB4A) can feature prominent granule neuron degeneration or hypomyelination, the literature directly studying pathogenic TUBA4A models points to Purkinje neuron loss as the hallmark driver of cerebellar pathology.

evidence.text: Tuba4a Q176P mutant mice exhibit normal development at 3 weeks of age, but by 30 days develop overt ataxia, extensive Purkinje neuron degeneration, and cerebellar atrophy, confirming time-dependent Purkinje cell loss after initial normal development as a central neurodegenerative driver of spastic ataxia.

source.title: A mouse model of autosomal dominant spastic ataxia and myopathy caused by a mutation in Tuba4a
source.quote: Mutant mice are normal at 3 weeks, except for decrement in muscle response following repetitive nerve stimulation. However, by 30 days these mice have overt ataxia, Purkinje neuron degeneration, and extensive skeletal muscle defects, which contribute to a decreased lifespan. Dominant TUBA4A mutations in humans are associated with spastic ataxia type 11 (SPAX11)...

evidence.text: In a series of 12 patients across 11 unrelated families harboring predicted pathogenic monoallelic TUBA4A missense variants, individuals presented with progressive spasticity and/or cerebellar ataxia associated with neurodegeneration and cerebellar alterations, confirming TUBA4A as an etiology of hereditary spastic ataxia with variable disease progression.

source.title: De novo and inherited monoallelic variants in TUBA4A cause ataxia and spasticity
source.quote: Taken together, we report 12 patients presenting with spasticity and/or cerebellar ataxia and harbouring a predicted pathogenic TUBA4A missense mutation, including five confirmed de novo cases and a mutation previously reported in a large family presenting with spastic ataxia.

evidence.text: A multigenerational family with 11 affected individuals and a second unrelated patient with the TUBA4A p.Glu415Lys mutation were characterized, identifying TUBA4A as a cause of dominantly inherited spastic ataxia associated with neurodegenerative microtubule disruption.

source.title: A new genetic cause of spastic ataxia: the p.Glu415Lys variant in TUBA4A
source.quote: In the present study, we report two families, one with 11 affected individuals and the other with a single patient, carrying a novel, likely pathogenic, variant (p. Glu415Lys) in the TUBA4A gene (NM_006000). The phenotype, not previously described, is that of spastic ataxia.

evidence.text: In other cerebellar tubulinopathies such as TUBB4A-related disease, cell death is selectively driven by cerebellar granule neuron degeneration rather than primary Purkinje degeneration, demonstrating that different tubulin isotypes exhibit divergent cellular tropism and histopathological drivers in the cerebellum.

source.title: A dominant tubulin mutation causes cerebellar neurodegeneration in a genetic model of tubulinopathy
source.quote: Here, we identify a mutation in the gene Tubb4a that causes degeneration of cerebellar granule neurons and myelination defects. We show that the neural phenotypes result from a cell type-specific enrichment of a dominant mutant form of Tubb4a relative to the expression other Β-tubulin isotypes.

new_directions.question_text: Does human post-mortem histopathology in SPAX11 patients demonstrate exclusive or primary Purkinje cell loss, or is there concurrent loss of granule neurons and deep cerebellar nuclei neurons?
new_directions.rationale: While animal models carrying Tuba4a missense mutations exhibit prominent selective Purkinje neuron degeneration, direct validation in post-mortem human cerebellar tissue across different disease durations is required to verify whether Purkinje loss is the sole primary driver of macrostructural cerebellar atrophy.

new_directions.question_text: Can volumetric 7T MRI of the cerebellar cortex distinguish Purkinje-layer predominant atrophy from granule cell layer atrophy in early-stage TUBA4A mutation carriers?
new_directions.rationale: Establishing high-resolution imaging biomarkers across early and late disease stages would clarify whether cortical cerebellar volume loss follows a spatiotemporal pattern reflecting initial Purkinje cell loss progressing to vermian and hemispheric atrophy.
